metadata.title: When Claude Audits a Spreadsheet, Does It Fix Anything?
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude finds AND fixes spreadsheet errors when it audits one -- or is doing something narrower. Lands the carry-out that audit-xls checks balance first, flags suspect formulas by cell, and never rewrites one -- fixing stays with the human.
metadata.source_note: Source sheet's narration carries real skill-specific facts (not unfilled template placeholders) -- see QUESTION.md. Facts preserved: the audit-xls skill audits a spreadsheet for formula accuracy, errors, and common mistakes; scopes to a selected range, a single sheet, or the entire model; checks BS balance first because everything downstream is suspect if it's off; triggers on phrases like 'audit this sheet' / 'check my formulas' / 'model won't balance'. beats.narration_text: People ask if Claude will just fix their broken spreadsheet. It won't. Liam here, in for Bear — let's take audit-xls apart and see what it actually does to that model.

beats.narration_text: Here's the intuitive guess. Audit-xls opens the spreadsheet, spots the broken formulas, and quietly rewrites them for you while it's in there. The skill doesn't work that way. It audits a sheet for formula accuracy, errors, and common mistakes — and then it reports what it finds, cited by cell. That's the whole job. Hand it a file with a formula you already know is broken, and open that file again after: the formula is untouched. What changed is the report, not the spreadsheet. They optimized for a traceable finding at the expense of the fix itself. Same sheet in, same sheet out — plus a list of where to look.

shot.new_visual_element: A 'fix it' hand reaching for a broken cell, struck through; a report card citing the same cell, lit

production_viz.label: Fix, struck -- report, lit
production_viz.mechanic: Left: a hand icon labelled 'FIX IT' reaching toward a cell marked with an error glyph. Right: a numbered card labelled 'AUDIT REPORT' listing 'cell: formula error, cited'. The fix-it side dims and gets a terracotta strike; the report side stays lit. A final line reads 'checked again -- cell unchanged' beside the same cell, still showing the original broken formula.

beats.narration_text: Here's the actual machinery. You point audit-xls at a scope — a range, one sheet, or the whole model — and the first thing it checks is whether the balance sheet balances. Not by accident. If BS is off, every downstream number is suspect, so there's no point auditing anything else until that check clears. Watch the anchor. A balance sheet off by twelve hundred dollars. Checked first. Mismatch found. The affected cells are cited. A finding is written to the report. And then it stops — nothing is rewritten, nothing is guessed at, the sheet stays exactly as you handed it over.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR -- a balance sheet mismatch traveling checked-first -> found -> cited -> reported, then stopping

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR -- one mismatch, four stops
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Four stacked cards labelled 'SCOPE SET', 'BS CHECKED FIRST', 'MISMATCH FOUND', 'CITED, REPORTED'. A single highlighted token 'BS OFF BY $1,200' travels down through all four cards in turn, each lighting as it arrives. At the bottom, the token halts beside a label 'nothing rewritten' -- it does not continue past the reported card. THIS EXACT COMPOSITION RETURNS, PAID OFF, AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Back to that balance sheet: cited, reported, waiting for a human to look. But read the flag carefully in both directions. A clean BS-balance pass doesn't mean the whole model is error-free — it clears one check. Formula errors elsewhere are audited separately, and only what you pointed the skill at got looked at. Going the other way, a BS-imbalance flag doesn't mean every downstream number is individually wrong. It means those numbers are unverified until the imbalance is resolved — not confirmed incorrect, just untrusted. Balanced isn't right. Off isn't wrong. And in both cases, nothing in the sheet has changed.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS, cited and reported; splits into 'balanced is not error-free' and 'suspect is not wrong'

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS -- reported, then split
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 FOUR-CARD COMPOSITION RETURNS, identical placement, the token resting at the 'CITED, REPORTED' card beside 'nothing rewritten'. It shrinks and slides up. Two cards fade in beneath: left reads 'BS: OK' with a checkmark, then a struck-through 'ERROR-FREE?' beneath it, labelled 'balanced is not error-free'; right reads 'BS: OFF' beside a faint 'unverified, not confirmed' note, labelled 'suspect is not wrong'.

beats.narration_text: Here's what audit-xls actually does: check the balance sheet first, then flag every suspect formula by cell. It never rewrites one. Finding the problem is the skill's job. Fixing it stays yours.

props.quote: Audit-xls checks the balance sheet first, then flags every suspect formula by cell — but it never rewrites one. Finding the problem is the skill's job. Fixing it stays yours.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini. Give it a tiny toy model with one formula you already know is broken and a balance sheet that's off by a fixed amount. Ask it to run the audit-xls skill on that scope: check whether the balance sheet balances first, then scan every formula for accuracy, errors, and common mistakes, then produce a cell-by-cell report. Tell it not to fix anything, and when it's done, ask it to confirm your original inputs are untouched. That's how you see the wiring — the audit runs, the report comes back, and the sheet doesn't move. Go deeper: describe a spreadsheet where audit-xls would return a clean BS-balance pass and no formula errors, but the model would still produce nonsense — and explain why the audit missed it. Liam, in for Bear.

llm_exercise.prompt: I want to see how the audit-xls skill actually works. Here is a tiny toy model with one deliberately broken formula and a balance sheet that is off by a fixed amount. Cells: A1 Revenue = 100000. A2 Cost of Goods = 40000. A3 Gross Profit = SUM(A1:A2)  [this is wrong — I meant subtraction, not sum]. A4 Operating Expense = 25000. A5 Net Income = A3 - A4. Side balance sheet: Assets = 80000, Liabilities = 20000, Equity = 55000 (off by 5000). Run the audit-xls skill on this scope: first, check whether the balance sheet balances; then scan every formula for accuracy, errors, and common mistakes; then produce a cell-by-cell report. Do not fix anything. When you finish, tell me exactly which cells you flagged, cite the specific error in each, and confirm that every one of my original input values is unchanged.
